name: Architectural Finishing (Blockwork, Plaster, Screed, Ceilings, Partitions, Painting)

activities: setting-out of block/partition lines to architectural grid
sequence.note: Finishing must not start on an unenclosed, wet, or unsurveyed shell; water ingress and structural movement void downstream finishes.

activities: one-side boarding of drywall (leave open for services)
sequence.note: Leave drywall single-sided until MEP first fix inside the cavity is complete and inspected.

sequence.stage: S3 - MEP first fix in walls (ENABLER)
activities: conduits, back-boxes, chases cut and made good
sequence.note: This is an MEP scope acting as a hold-point for plaster; chasing after plaster is rework and is prohibited on quality plans.

activities: render to wet-area walls (cementitious background for tiling)
sequence.note: Wet-area walls receive a cementitious/water-resistant background, NOT gypsum plaster, because tiling and waterproofing follow.

activities: underfloor heating or conduit encased first
sequence.note: Screed must reach the specified moisture content before any adhered floor finish; premature covering traps moisture.

sequence.stage: S6 - Ceiling framing & MEP above-ceiling coordination
activities: ceiling grid/MF framing set to level
hold for above-ceiling ductwork/tray/pipe first fix + insulation + pressure/leak tests
first layer boarding once services signed off
sequence.note: Do not close the ceiling until every above-ceiling service is installed, tested, and inspected; reopening is major rework.

activities: filler and first finish coats to walls and ceilings
sequence.note: First coats only until wet works and dust-generating trades are clear; final coat is deferred.

sequence.stage: S9 - Final paint / touch-up (after second fix)
sequence.note: Final decoration is the last wet trade; it closes after joinery, fixtures, and second-fix MEP so damage is captured once.

typical_relationships.reason: plaster requires a stable, complete, dimensionally-set substrate; plastering a partial or unsettled wall cracks and delaminates
conduits, back-boxes and concealed pipe must be buried and inspected before the wall is sealed; chasing finished plaster is rework

typical_relationships.before: all wet works (plaster, screed, render curing)
typical_relationships.reason: residual construction moisture and alkalinity cause efflorescence, blistering and adhesion failure of paint
closing the ceiling before services are complete and tested forces destructive reopening for access or leak repair
adhered finishes over green screed debond and trap moisture; skirting set on damp screed wicks and stains
final decoration captures all preceding damage in a single touch-up pass; painting first guarantees rework
airborne dust embeds in wet paint film

interfaces.requirement: conduit, back-boxes and concealed pipe installed, chased and inspected before plaster / drywall close-up (architecture-MEP first-fix handshake)
ductwork, cable tray, containment, piping and insulation installed and pressure/leak tested before ceiling boarding; access panels coordinated to valves/dampers/VAVs
floor conduit/UFH/drainage stub-ups fixed and, where required, tested before screed pour
slab handed over, surveyed and to tolerance; building watertight before any internal finishing starts
external envelope closed and weathertight to protect internal wet trades
final paint coat released only after wiring devices, grilles/diffusers and fixtures are terminated so touch-up is single-pass

commissioning_dependencies: screed moisture test passed before floor finish
permanent HVAC or dehumidification available to dry the building before final paint
protection regime in place before handover
testing_requirements: screed surface regularity (straightedge / SR rating) and moisture content (hygrometer / CM)
paint DFT / coverage and colour/sheen approval on benchmark
fire-rated partition and ceiling penetration / integrity check
typical_exceptions: exposed-services (no ceiling) design - above-ceiling MEP handshake becomes a coordinated finished-services exposure, painted/wrapped
fair-faced concrete or exposed blockwork - plaster stage omitted, joint/repair and sealer only
access-floor systems replace screed in data/office - pedestal floor after underfloor services
dry-lining on dabs instead of wet plaster shortens drying but needs level substrate

work_packages.note: gated by MEP wall first fix
split first/final coats around second fix

evidence: Universal building-finishing constructability logic on residential, commercial and industrial fit-out: masonry/partition -> MEP wall first fix -> plaster -> screed -> ceiling (after above-ceiling MEP test) -> paint, with wet-trade moisture control gating decoration. Terminology generalized; no project-specific data.
